medad_1977.name: Medad
medad_1977.who: One of Israel's seventy elders who prophesied in the camp when the Spirit rested on him in the wilderness.
key: Medad was registered among the seventy elders but remained in the camp instead of going to the tent (Numbers 11).
The Spirit rested on Medad and Eldad, and they prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11).
When Joshua urged Moses to stop them, Moses wished all the LORD's people were prophets (Numbers 11).

melech_1993.name: Melech
melech_1993.who: A son of Micah and great-grandson of Jonathan, listed in the genealogy of King Saul's family.
key: Melech is listed as a son of Micah, son of Merib-baal, in Saul's line through Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8).
The genealogy of Saul's descendants is repeated, again naming Melech among Micah's sons (1 Chronicles 9).

meonothai_1998.name: Meonothai
meonothai_1998.who: A son of Othniel, Israel's first judge, listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
key: Meonothai is named with his brother Hathath as a son of Othniel (1 Chronicles 4).
He fathered Ophrah, continuing Othniel's family line in Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

merodach-baladan_483.name: Merodach-baladan
merodach-baladan_483.who: A king of Babylon, son of Baladan, who sent envoys to King Hezekiah after Hezekiah recovered from illness.
key: Hearing of Hezekiah's illness and recovery, he sent envoys with letters and a gift (Isaiah 39).
Hezekiah welcomed the envoys and showed them all the treasures in his storehouses (Isaiah 39).
Isaiah then foretold that everything Hezekiah had shown would be carried off to Babylon (Isaiah 39).
The same visit is recorded in the account of Hezekiah's reign (2 Kings 20).

mesha_2009.name: Mesha
mesha_2009.who: A king of Moab, a sheep breeder who paid tribute to Israel and rebelled after Ahab's death.
key: Mesha paid Israel's king a heavy yearly tribute of lambs and wool (2 Kings 3).
After Ahab died, Mesha rebelled, and the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom marched against him (2 Kings 3).
His army was routed after mistaking water in the valley for blood (2 Kings 3).
Failing to break through, he offered his eldest son as a burnt offering on the city wall (2 Kings 3).

meshullam_2024.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2024.who: A Benjaminite, son of Hodaviah, whose son Sallu lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile.
key: Meshullam is listed as son of Hodaviah in the genealogy of the Benjaminites (1 Chronicles 9).
His son Sallu was among the Benjaminites who settled in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).

meshullam_2025.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2025.who: A Benjaminite, son of Shephatiah, who was a head of a father's house living in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Meshullam son of Shephatiah is listed among the Benjaminites living in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
He was counted among the heads of fathers' houses in their families (1 Chronicles 9).

meshullam_2026.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2026.who: A priest of the house of Immer, son of Meshillemith, named in the ancestry of a priest serving in Jerusalem.
key: Meshullam son of Meshillemith appears in the ancestry of the priest Maasai, of the house of Immer (1 Chronicles 9).
His descendants were among the priests who lived in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).

meshullam_2036.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2036.who: A Benjaminite, son of Joed, whose son Sallu settled in Jerusalem in Nehemiah's day.
key: Meshullam is listed as son of Joed in the line of the Benjaminites (Nehemiah 11).
His son Sallu was among the leaders of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).

micah_2053.name: Micah
micah_2053.who: A prophet from Moresheth who warned Samaria and Jerusalem of judgment and foretold a ruler from Bethlehem.
key: Micah prophesied in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, concerning Samaria and Jerusalem (Micah 1).
He warned that because of corrupt leaders, Zion would be plowed as a field (Micah 3).
He foretold a ruler for Israel coming from Bethlehem Ephrathah (Micah 5).
He declared that the LORD requires justice, kindness, and walking humbly with God (Micah 6).
Years later, elders cited his warning to spare Jeremiah's life (Jeremiah 26).

mishael_2090.name: Mishael
mishael_2090.who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, son of Uzziel and cousin of Moses and Aaron.
key: Mishael is listed as a son of Uzziel, son of Kohath, with Elzaphan and Sithri (Exodus 6).
After Nadab and Abihu died, Moses had Mishael and Elzaphan carry their bodies out of the camp (Leviticus 10).

mizzah_2101.name: Mizzah
mizzah_2101.who: A grandson of Esau through his son Reuel, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Mizzah was a son of Reuel, Esau's son by Basemath (Genesis 36).
He is named among the chiefs of the sons of Reuel in Edom (Genesis 36).
His name is repeated in the genealogy of Esau's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

nadab_2129.name: Nadab
nadab_2129.who: A son of Jeroboam who reigned over Israel for two years before Baasha assassinated him.
key: Nadab succeeded his father Jeroboam as king of Israel (1 Kings 14).
He reigned two years and did evil, walking in his father's sin (1 Kings 15).
Baasha conspired against him and killed him while Israel besieged Gibbethon (1 Kings 15).
Baasha then struck down Jeroboam's whole house, as the prophet Ahijah had foretold (1 Kings 15).

naharai_2135.name: Naharai
naharai_2135.who: A man of Beeroth who served as armor-bearer to Joab and was listed among David's mighty men.
key: Naharai of Beeroth, Joab's armor-bearer, is named among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
The parallel list of David's mighty men again names him as Joab's armor-bearer (1 Chronicles 11).

nahash_2136.name: Nahash
nahash_2136.who: A king of the Ammonites whose siege of Jabesh-gilead led to Saul's first victory as king.
key: Nahash besieged Jabesh-gilead and demanded to gouge out every man's right eye as terms (1 Samuel 11).
The Spirit of God rushed on Saul, who rallied Israel and defeated the Ammonites (1 Samuel 11).
Samuel later recalled that Israel demanded a king when they saw Nahash coming against them (1 Samuel 12).

nahash_2137.name: Nahash
nahash_2137.who: A king of the Ammonites who showed kindness to David and was succeeded by his son Hanun.
key: Nahash had dealt kindly with David, so David sent servants to console Hanun when Nahash died (2 Samuel 10).
Hanun shamed David's envoys, leading to war between Ammon and Israel (2 Samuel 10).
The same events are recorded in the account of David's wars (1 Chronicles 19).

nahath_2146.name: Nahath
nahath_2146.who: A grandson of Esau through his son Reuel, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Nahath was a son of Reuel, Esau's son by Basemath (Genesis 36).
He is named among the chiefs of the sons of Reuel in Edom (Genesis 36).
His name is repeated in the genealogy of Esau's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

nahum_2145.name: Nahum
nahum_2145.who: A prophet from Elkosh whose book announces the LORD's judgment on Nineveh, the Assyrian capital.
key: Nahum of Elkosh received a vision concerning Nineveh (Nahum 1).
He proclaimed the LORD slow to anger yet sure to punish the guilty (Nahum 1).
He announced good news of peace for Judah, whose Assyrian yoke would be broken (Nahum 1).
He described the attack on Nineveh and the plundering of the city (Nahum 2).
He compared Nineveh to Thebes, which also fell despite its defenses (Nahum 3).

nathan_2154.name: Nathan
nathan_2154.who: A man of Zobah whose son Igal and brother Joel are named among David's mighty men.
key: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
The parallel list names Joel the brother of Nathan among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

nebo_2166.name: Nebo
nebo_2166.who: A town in Judah whose people returned from exile, not an individual person.
key: Men of Nebo are counted among the returning exiles (Ezra 2).
Some descendants of Nebo had married foreign women and agreed to put them away (Ezra 10).

nehemiah_2171.name: Nehemiah
nehemiah_2171.who: A leader who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel, distinct from the later governor Nehemiah.
key: Nehemiah is named among the leaders who came up from exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
Nehemiah's register of the first returnees lists him again among those leaders (Nehemiah 7).

nehemiah_2173.name: Nehemiah
nehemiah_2173.who: Son of Azbuk and ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall.
key: As ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, he repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
His work reached opposite David's tombs, the artificial pool, and the house of the mighty men (Nehemiah 3).

nemuel_2177.name: Nemuel
nemuel_2177.who: A Reubenite, son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram.
key: Nemuel is listed as a son of Eliab, of Pallu's clan in the tribe of Reuben (Numbers 26).
His brothers Dathan and Abiram joined Korah's rebellion against Moses and perished (Numbers 26).

nepheg_2178.name: Nepheg
nepheg_2178.who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, son of Izhar and brother of Korah.
key: Nepheg is listed as a son of Izhar, a grandson of Kohath, in the Levite genealogy (Exodus 6).
His brother Korah later led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).

nimrod_2206.name: Nimrod
nimrod_2206.who: A son of Cush, the first mighty man on earth and a great hunter, who founded cities in Shinar and Assyria.
key: Nimrod, son of Cush, became the first mighty man on earth, a mighty hunter before the LORD (Genesis 10).
His kingdom began with Babel, Erech, and Accad in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10).
From there he went into Assyria and built Nineveh and other cities (Genesis 10).
Micah later called Assyria the land of Nimrod (Micah 5).

noah_2211.name: Noah
noah_2211.who: One of the five daughters of Zelophehad, who asked Moses for their father's inheritance in Manasseh.
key: Noah is listed among Zelophehad's daughters, since he had no sons (Numbers 26).
She and her sisters asked Moses for their father's inheritance, and the LORD granted it (Numbers 27).
As commanded, the sisters married within their father's clan so the land stayed in Manasseh (Numbers 36).
The sisters received their inheritance among the clans of Manasseh (Joshua 17).

obadiah_2226.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2226.who: A prophet whose short book, the shortest in the Old Testament, announces God's judgment on Edom.
key: Obadiah's vision announces that proud Edom, secure in its rocky heights, will be brought down (Obadiah 1).
He condemns Edom for gloating and violence against its brother Jacob when Jerusalem fell (Obadiah 1).
He declares the day of the LORD near and that the kingdom will be the LORD's (Obadiah 1).

oded_2237.name: Oded
oded_2237.who: A prophet in Samaria who persuaded Israel's army to free the captives taken from Judah under King Ahaz.
key: Oded met Israel's army returning to Samaria with two hundred thousand captives from Judah (2 Chronicles 28).
He warned that God was angry and that the captives must be sent back (2 Chronicles 28).
Ephraimite leaders backed him, and the captives were clothed, fed, and returned to Jericho (2 Chronicles 28).

omar_2242.name: Omar
omar_2242.who: A grandson of Esau through his son Eliphaz, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Omar was a son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn by Adah (Genesis 36).
He is named among the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in Edom (Genesis 36).
His name is repeated in the genealogy of Esau's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

onam_2248.name: Onam
onam_2248.who: A son of Shobal, of the Horite clans who lived in the land of Seir.
key: Onam is listed among the sons of Shobal, a son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
His name is repeated in the genealogy of the people of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

onam_2249.name: Onam
onam_2249.who: A son of Jerahmeel and his wife Atarah, in the tribe of Judah.
key: Onam was born to Jerahmeel by another wife, Atarah (1 Chronicles 2).
He fathered Shammai and Jada, through whom the Jerahmeelite line continues (1 Chronicles 2).

onesimus_2251.name: Onesimus
onesimus_2251.who: A slave of Philemon who became a Christian through Paul and was sent back as a brother.
key: Onesimus came to faith through Paul while Paul was in prison (Philemon 1).
Paul sent him back to Philemon, once useless but now useful, as a beloved brother (Philemon 1).
Paul offered to repay anything Onesimus owed Philemon (Philemon 1).
Paul sent him with Tychicus to Colossae, calling him faithful and beloved (Colossians 4).

onesiphorus_2252.name: Onesiphorus
onesiphorus_2252.who: A believer who often refreshed Paul and sought him out in Rome during his imprisonment.
key: Unlike others who turned away, Onesiphorus was not ashamed of Paul's chains (2 Timothy 1).
He searched for Paul in Rome until he found him (2 Timothy 1).
Paul recalled his many services at Ephesus and prayed for mercy on his household (2 Timothy 1).
Paul asked Timothy to greet the household of Onesiphorus (2 Timothy 4).

ophir_2253.name: Ophir
ophir_2253.who: A son of Joktan in the line of Shem, listed in the Table of Nations.
key: Ophir is named among the thirteen sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem (Genesis 10).
Joktan's sons lived from Mesha toward Sephar, the hill country of the east (Genesis 10).
His name is repeated in the genealogy from Adam to Abraham (1 Chronicles 1).

oreb_2255.name: Oreb
oreb_2255.who: A prince of Midian captured and killed by the Ephraimites during Gideon's victory over Midian.
key: After Gideon's rout of Midian, the Ephraimites captured Oreb and killed him at the rock of Oreb (Judges 7).
They brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan (Judges 7).
Gideon calmed Ephraim's anger by noting God had given them Oreb and Zeeb (Judges 8).
Later psalmists and prophets recalled his defeat as a pattern of God's judgment (Psalm 83; Isaiah 10).

oren_2256.name: Oren
oren_2256.who: A son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, in the tribe of Judah.
key: Oren is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Ram, Bunah, Ozem, and Ahijah, and his half-brother was Onam (1 Chronicles 2).

orpah_2257.name: Orpah
orpah_2257.who: A Moabite woman, daughter-in-law of Naomi, who returned to her own people instead of going to Bethlehem.
key: Orpah married one of Naomi's sons while the family lived in Moab (Ruth 1).
After her husband died, she set out with Naomi and Ruth toward Judah (Ruth 1).
At Naomi's urging, Orpah kissed her goodbye and went back to her people and gods (Ruth 1).

ozem_2260.name: Ozem
ozem_2260.who: The sixth son of Jesse and an older brother of King David.
key: Ozem is named as Jesse's sixth son, with David listed as the seventh (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers included Eliab, Abinadab, and Shimea, and his sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail (1 Chronicles 2).

ozem_2261.name: Ozem
ozem_2261.who: A son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, in the tribe of Judah.
key: Ozem is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Ram, Bunah, Oren, and Ahijah, and his half-brother was Onam (1 Chronicles 2).

paruah_2278.name: Paruah
paruah_2278.who: The father of Jehoshaphat, one of King Solomon's twelve district officers.
key: Paruah is named as father of Jehoshaphat in the list of Solomon's officers (1 Kings 4).
His son Jehoshaphat supplied food for the king's household from Issachar (1 Kings 4).

pekahiah_2300.name: Pekahiah
pekahiah_2300.who: A son of Menahem who reigned over Israel two years before his officer Pekah assassinated him.
key: Pekahiah succeeded his father Menahem as king of Israel (2 Kings 15).
He reigned two years in Samaria and did evil, following Jeroboam's sins (2 Kings 15).
His captain Pekah son of Remaliah conspired with fifty Gileadites and killed him in the palace citadel (2 Kings 15).

pelatiah_2307.name: Pelatiah
pelatiah_2307.who: A son of Benaiah and leader in Jerusalem who died suddenly while Ezekiel prophesied against the city's wicked leaders.
key: Ezekiel saw Pelatiah among twenty-five men at the temple gate giving wicked counsel (Ezekiel 11).
While Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah died, and Ezekiel fell on his face crying out to God (Ezekiel 11).

peninnah_2313.name: Peninnah
peninnah_2313.who: A wife of Elkanah who had children and provoked his childless wife Hannah year after year.
key: Elkanah had two wives, and Peninnah had children while Hannah had none (1 Samuel 1).
At the yearly sacrifice in Shiloh, Elkanah gave portions to Peninnah and her children (1 Samuel 1).
Peninnah provoked Hannah severely, so that Hannah wept and would not eat (1 Samuel 1).

pharaoh_2328.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2328.who: The unnamed king of Egypt who took Sarai into his household when Abram went to Egypt during a famine.
key: Pharaoh's officials praised Sarai, and she was taken into his house, believed to be Abram's sister (Genesis 12).
Pharaoh treated Abram well for her sake, giving him livestock and servants (Genesis 12).
The LORD struck Pharaoh's house with great plagues because of Sarai (Genesis 12).
Pharaoh rebuked Abram and sent him away with his wife and possessions (Genesis 12).

pharaoh_2335.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2335.who: The king of Egypt named among the rulers who must drink the cup of the LORD's wrath in Jeremiah's prophecy.
key: Jeremiah's prophecy of the cup is dated to Jehoiakim's fourth year, Nebuchadnezzar's first (Jeremiah 25).
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his officials, and his people are named among the nations to drink it (Jeremiah 25).
In that same year Nebuchadnezzar defeated Pharaoh Neco's army at Carchemish (Jeremiah 46).

philemon_2342.name: Philemon
philemon_2342.who: A believer whose house hosted a church and to whom Paul wrote, appealing for his slave Onesimus.
key: Paul greeted Philemon as a beloved fellow worker, with the church meeting in his house (Philemon 1).
Paul thanked God for Philemon's love and faith, which refreshed the hearts of the saints (Philemon 1).
Paul urged him to receive Onesimus back as a beloved brother, not merely a slave (Philemon 1).
Paul offered to repay any debt and asked Philemon to prepare him a guest room (Philemon 1).

piram_2361.name: Piram
piram_2361.who: A king of Jarmuth who joined four other Amorite kings against Gibeon and was defeated by Joshua.
key: Adoni-zedek of Jerusalem asked Piram to join an attack on Gibeon for making peace with Israel (Joshua 10).
Joshua defeated the five kings, who hid in a cave at Makkedah and were then executed (Joshua 10).

pithon_2363.name: Pithon
pithon_2363.who: A son of Micah and great-grandson of Jonathan, listed in the genealogy of King Saul's family.
key: Pithon is listed first among the sons of Micah, son of Merib-baal, in Saul's line (1 Chronicles 8).
The genealogy of Saul's descendants is repeated, again naming Pithon (1 Chronicles 9).

potiphar_2368.name: Potiphar
potiphar_2368.who: An Egyptian officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, who bought Joseph as a slave.
key: Potiphar bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites who had brought him to Egypt (Genesis 39).
Seeing the LORD was with Joseph, he put him in charge of his whole household (Genesis 39).
The LORD blessed Potiphar's house for Joseph's sake (Genesis 39).
When his wife falsely accused Joseph, Potiphar put him in the king's prison (Genesis 39).

puah_2372.name: Puah
puah_2372.who: A Hebrew midwife in Egypt who, with Shiphrah, feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew baby boys.
key: Pharaoh ordered Puah and Shiphrah to kill every Hebrew boy at birth (Exodus 1).
Fearing God, the midwives let the boys live and gave Pharaoh an explanation (Exodus 1).
God dealt well with the midwives and gave them families of their own (Exodus 1).

publius_2374.name: Publius
publius_2374.who: The chief official of Malta, who welcomed Paul after his shipwreck and whose father Paul healed.
key: Publius welcomed Paul and his companions and hosted them for three days (Acts 28).
Paul prayed for Publius's father, sick with fever and dysentery, and healed him (Acts 28).
Afterward the rest of the island's sick came and were cured (Acts 28).

raamah_2380.name: Raamah
raamah_2380.who: A son of Cush and grandson of Ham, whose sons Sheba and Dedan are listed in the Table of Nations.
key: Raamah is named among the sons of Cush, son of Ham (Genesis 10).
He fathered Sheba and Dedan (Genesis 10).
Traders of Raamah later dealt in spices, precious stones, and gold with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
